The steam release has been my first experience with RE3 and it's been a fascinating playthrough. It's surprising how different the locations are from the remake. The depiction of Raccoon City here deeply captures the atmosphere of a metropolis succumbing to chaos and terror. Overwhelming zombie forces litter the labyrinth of streets and buildings, while the last remaining survivors are isolated and hunted down. Visiting the RPD as Jill simply felt more impactful. And the Clock Tower and Disposal Plant locations felt so atmospheric and memorable that I can understand why fans were upset the remake did not include them.

That said, this game is the most difficult RE game I've played, and it's mostly due to the boss fights. Tank controls just feel ill equipped for confronting a fast paced Nemesis who will sprint at you and aggressively lock you down with multiple attacks. While the game adds a quick turn and dodge mechanic to help, the fights still felt very clunky to me. Easily my most disliked aspect of this game. Thankfully most of the Nemesis encounters can be ran from.

Ultimately if you're curious about the original RE3, give this game a try. It can be comfortably completed over a weekend.

You could make a convincing argument that the remakes of RE 1 or 2 are better than their original counterparts, but this is inarguably better to it's remake. Here's a short list of things this game has that 3 remake is lacking:
- Nemesis shows up more, is tougher to defeat, and drops more unique items (Parts for fully new guns, etc.)
- Fuller city streets section that you return to several times, complete with rewards for observant explorers using new items
- Semi-random enemy layouts in some rooms (Remake only mixes up enemy arrangements for each difficulty, the original does it in most every room in it's back half)
- Branching story moments that can even dictate Nemesis encounters, such as meeting Carlos in the restaurant or press office, and where Tyrus dies later on
- Split second decision moments (These are so simple their exclusion from the remake must have just been laziness)
- An ENTIRE section at the clock tower with several puzzles and multiple Nemesis encounters
- An ENTIRE section at the Raccoon City park with tons of enemies and a few puzzles
- The GIANT T-VIRUS WORM boss fight (The fight is kinda bad and would have been perfect material for the remake to improve)
And that list isn't even totally comprehensive. Furthermore, I'd say that the remake is the shortest single campaign of the remake trilogy, while this has the longest single campaign of the classic trilogy. tl;dr, the remake is not a very good reflection of how great this game is, and I think you should play this instead. Without spoiling anything, it's excellent, even better then OG RE2 in some regards.

After being thoroughly disappointed and disillusioned with the state of the Resident Evil 3 remake, sitting and playing the original game has only made me lament what we could have had. The original Resident Evil 3 Nemesis is a phenomenal game, from start to finish, and worthy of being one of the icons of the survival horror genre. Do yourself a service, embrace those crunchy PS1 graphics and funny voice work, and experience a true horror like no other (and don't let anyone try and say fixed cameras and tank controls are "outdated" or "bad", not only are they great fun but they enhance the game with their inclusion)

Something that RE3 excels at is mixing together a blend of both haunting, somber ambience with truly terrifying moments of action to create an unforgettable environment. The introductory cutscenes do a great job at building suspense and showing you just how screwed everything is. Police and militant forces alike are rendered useless at the sheer might and volume of infected zombies. After that, you're thrown right into the chaos, forced to battle for your life, and that is when you get a proper taste of the setting. The streets of Raccoon City are desolate, robbed of all natural life and left with nothing but infected, shambling corpses. Cars and buildings burning to rubble. You even get to visit the RPD early on, with nothing but a few zombies as remnants of what used to be there. It is so lonely, and that feeling of being alone with monsters help build into the suspense and dread that lingers throughout the game. This is all heightened with the different moment to moment occurrences that keep you on your toes. I'd like to preface part of this note by saying that I am a huge scaredy-cat, and a lot of horror games can really mess me up. But the chills I felt when the growls of a zombie echo offscreen, leaving me wondering if I was about to walk head-first into danger, was great. Or if a hallway I had traversed many times before suddenly exploding and being flooded by a fresh wave of infected. Even worse, when Nemesis came barreling around a corner to deck me in the face was equal parts scary and elating. On the topic of Nemesis...

Now THAT is how you do a stalker enemy! The remake really dumbed him down and turned him into a glorified mini-boss that you can kill with a grenade or two. He served as nothing more than an obnoxious obstacle that could be swept away with little effort. Here, he is ultra fast, hits like a freight train, and his appearances feel both unpredictable and terrifying! Add onto the fact that the tank controls take away a degree of power from you, and any encounter with Nemmy feels like a true struggle for your life. Especially with his arsenal and constantly ability to reappear and follow you anywhere. Too close? He's gonna swing and punch you right in the face. Too far, and he might whip out a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ROCKET LAUNCHER. Nemesis is the embodiment of a relentless killing machine, and his very presence elevates RE3 into an amazing survival experience. I know stalker type enemies are not everyone's cup of tea, but I feel that the game would be sorely lacking without his presence. Part of the fear and charm of RE3 is the random appearances of this stapled-face ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and I love it

Player agency is another key contributor to the legendary status of RE3. The remake ended up stripping this away and making the game mind-numbingly linear (which isn't necessarily a bad thing, linear games CAN and HAVE been done right, but I think in the case of RE3R it missed the mark). But in the OG, your choices impact how the story plays out. Not just with clearly defined choices in cutscenes, but even moment to moment gameplay of choosing which location to investigate first that still impacts the story in a meaningful way. Do you decide to check out the restaurant, or the newspaper office first, and have different encounters with different choices? Do you actively engage Nemesis in a risky battle that will require a majority of your resources, or duck for safety and save them for smaller grunts or future boss fights? Having the choice to do things just feels nice. Raccoon City is a very twisty-turny city with a lot of different routes to explore and navigate, and it makes the player feel good when they get to deviate from a more obvious path in search of goodies. 

Music also plays an important role in reinforcing the feeling of RE3. I feel this is best showcased within the RPD. At first, you are met with this majestic tune in the lobby. It is relaxing and calm and lulls you into a false sense of security within the walls of the police station. Then, you duck into the halls, and the music turns creepy and low. Enough to keep you on edge but not much more than that. But then, with the introduction of Nemesis, the music picks up. It starts looming over you, playing this offputting song that lets you know you are not safe anywhere. Even the tune of the safe room is overwritten by this song that just evokes dread. It is superb, the way music is utilized.

And of course, if you couldn't get enough of that delicious RE3 goodness, you can jump into Mercenaries and have some fun there. It leans way more into the action than any scare factor, but its a great change of pace. Like every version of Mercs that came after it, you get a set time limit to kill enemies, with each enemy killed adding to your timer. Although, here it is much less arcadey compared to something like RE4, instead needing you to run from one end of the map to the other. The three different mercs all fill different strengths, and they all feel like a blast to play. Doing all this lets you earn some rewards, being infinite ammo weapons of increasing strength. It may not be my favourite iteration of the mode, but its still great fun and paved the way for future RE games to expand on it

RE3 has left me with mixed feelings. I absolutely adored the first half of the game. Running through the streets of Raccoon City as the Nemesis is constantly breathing in your neck is one of the highlights of the franchise. Speaking of that area, that's where you can also find some of the best puzzles, level design, encounters and atmosphere in the entire franchise, truly unforgettable experience. The second half of the game left a bad taste in my mouth however. From the moment you take control of Carlos, everything starts to fall apart. Environments, enemies and tasks become very repetitive. The puzzles get progressively worse as most of them from that point on are the 'Press Random Buttons Untill You Figure Out The Pattern Or Accidentally Complete The Puzzle' type. The entire 'Carlos' section is a pace killer. The final area of the game is completely unnecessary, and it's just there to drag out. The final confrontation with the Nemesis is indescribably awkward and frustrating. All of those issues might not be a big deal if isolated, but stack them up, and they make a ten out of ten game go down to an eight. It's a shame really, because if the second part was as good as the first, RE3 would have easily been my favourite in the franchise. Either way, the original is infinitely better then the Remake in every regard, except of course in graphics and audio quality. I would still recommend playing both versions however, as they are fundamentally different games and offer very different experiences.

I was praying that the classic RE trilogy came to Steam, especially as it's the 30th anniversary and was bummed on the actual day when there was radio silence on anything RE. Then on the morning on April 2nd I opened Twitter and saw tweets about RE being dropped on Steam - and I legit thought it was some late April Fools joke but ofc I went for the bait and it was true!!! Ofc I instantly bought the trilogy. I have these releases on GOG and actually first time dove into RE1 and RE2 and thought they were so much fun.

Now RE3 has always been a special game to me as it was the 2nd RE game I played way back in 2012/13 after finishing RE4 (Gamecube) on my Nintendo Wii and I loved it as a kid and always placed it as my 2nd fav of the franchise until I played the remakes of RE1, 2 and 4 that is.

So this is my 1st replay since being a kid and it holds up so damn well just like RE1 and RE2 do but this one is so me, it's faster paced - you don't stay in 1 area for too long - and feels like a great final entry in the Raccoon City trilogy as Jill makes her last escape - and it feels just like it.

I LOVE the streets of RC - they look perfect in the sense of a zombie outbreak, and are designed and loop well - the Uptown, Downtown areas are solid but then ofc we get to visit the RPD which is always a treat - but again, not too much time is spent there as ofc it was featured heavily in RE2. Then the CLOCK TOWER, just a great iconic location and fits right in there will the franchise as well as the hospital and factory areas - which again is a HUGE miss for the remake.

This game is a LOT shorter in length than RE2, but funnily enough, it's maybe a bit longer than RE3 Remake but it works because we get a great variety of locations, enemy types and weaponry and it all just fits so well man. The score is also a banger too.

Now ofc there is the NEMESIS who is easily my favourite monster in the franchise - he genuinely feels like he is stalking you throughout the entiriety of the game, and the game doesn't go on for too long without his presence - and whenever he shows up it is always intense. The way he runs at you, shoots rockets - it's just so damn good - and is one of the BIGGEST reasons why the remake missed the mark as most of his parts were heavily scripted. I absolutely LOVE the live choice selection because it instantly encourages replayability and changes certain scenarios around - its great because we only get to play Jill's story and its a smart way for them to encourage repeat playthroughs.

I love the introduction of the gunpowder system which allows crafting of ammunition (it is VERY VERY generous with how much ammo you get as well as herbs and ink ribbons on HARD mode - I had so much excess by the end lmao). It's just such a damn brilliant sequel to RE2 and a brilliant ending to the trilogy.

This is, hands down, the best fixed camera RE game. On top of having good resource management, puzzles and exploration, it has very satisfying combat. Even though mechanically it is the same as previous games, there is something about its weapons, sound effects and enemy reactions that make it way more fun than RE1 and 2. RE3 embraces its action and puts a lot of emphasis on it via interesting enemy designs and combat situations while retaining its survival horror roots. And it still has THE BEST crafting system of any RE game. Using gunpowder has so much depth it can help create a unique playstyle each time you revisit it. You wanna focus on your pistol and shotgun, slowly learning to craft enhanced ammo? Go for it. You wanna create a bunch of different grenade rounds to blast zombies into oblivion? Go for it. You wanna mix and match different types of ammo? Go for it. 

This is also the first RE game that introduced creative designs to its boss encounters. Grave Digger fight, treatment plant Nemesis, final Nemesis - all of these fights are designed in a way to beat them with using little to no ammo.

I cannot recommend this game enough. The steam version is fine, but I recommend converting it to the sourcenext version and using the classic rebirth patch. Without it, it has atrocious 3d model warping that looks horrendous.

P.S. Do not mind my 15 minute playtime. When you convert it to Sourcenext version and launch it from the folder, Steam does not recognise you playing it. My playtime of this game across 27 years is close to 500 hours xD

While the dynamic between Carlos and Jill was an interesting point, and the desperation between the two to get tf out of Racoon City, narratively, I did not have that much of an investment as I did with the RE2 story. It did still help me stay with the game, but I will remember this game for its gameplay more then its story. What I did enjoy was the tension between the group and Nikolai, as while the betrayal wasn't that surprising, I did enjoy his role of being the mole in the group, having ulterior motives, and just overall being a massive ♥♥♥♥, killing members without explaining it to Jill or Carlos. The main thing to takeaway from RE3 is what was occurring on the streets during Racoon City... pure and total chaos, I am so sorry you had to have Nemesis chasing you the entire game Jill lmao.

Characters
The characters are the better aspect of RE3, not the story. Jill and Carlos have a pretty good story arc, with Jill's desperation running away from Nemesis being super fun to experience. I do wish that There were more times when they stuck together, as the game had them separate for 95% of the game, but the few times they do connect I did enjoy the most, even if he never shows up ever again in future titles. While most RE games have the characters trying to uncover the greater Mystery, Jill... honestly don't even care about what Umbrella is since she already knew about it back in RE1, she just wants to live. It is a funny refresher cause literally every other RE game is mystery unsolving, but nah Jill don't give af about any of that LMAO. I did like the segments with Carlos trying to hard to cure Jill after she gets infected, easily my favorite character moment between them. Overall The cast was pretty cool, but not my favorite of the original RE trilogy.

Gameplay
This is what people talk about when it comes to the big 3. Honestly, yeah, RE3 gameplay is pretty good, but apart from Nemesis, I think that comes from the fact that they give you SO MUCH ammo, that resource management never really became an issue for me even on hard mode. However, Those nemesis sections were just so damn good that its easy to see why its so beloved. I do think that RE3 was pretty easy overall cause without the resource management, its pretty easy to blast through hordes. The boss fights however is when the game does become challenging. The nemesis fights especially leave you with little breathing room, so you do have to learn the dodge mechanic to deal with him. The dodge mechanic speaking of is quite frankly, mixed? I love the addition as it adds to the more action oriented focus of RE3, and when it works boy does it feel good. However, the dodge mechanic has some major flaws to it. One, its mapped to the same button as aiming, meaning to dodge, you have to time your aim. What that causes is not only unintentional dodging, but moments where after you dodge, your character randomly aims again, causing you to get hit again. The game also doesn't really  balance the dodge mechanic, as some enemies like zombies don't have telegraphed attacks, so you just have to know when they attack. Nemesis thankfully, is pretty telegraphed so thats when the dodge mechanic shines. The tank controls, I didn't mind. I like these classic controls and it does add to the horror element, when it does feel painful is when you are bum rushed by bosses and have to turn around, but get staggered in between. Apart from that, I like RE3 gameplay, even if I wish it was more difficult.

Music
A ton of reused songs from classic RE games, but overall I did enjoy it. A ton of the song just add to the fact you are exploring a ruined city, people screaming, gunshots everywhere and just overall chaos. The obvious songs being city of ruin and city without hope. The song to get the most out of me is easily Nemesis theme, every time that song played while I was exploring oh my GOD the chills that went through my spines felt so damn good.

Last positives/Nitpicks
-The PC port is barebones, don't expect anything more then what you would get from emulation. Default Keyboard controls are also hilariously bad so rebind those asap.
- Fullscreen crashed way too often, switching to Windowed mode fixed that.
- It is way too easy to accidentally skip cutscenes, so many times I had to look up a longplay cause I tapped interact while running or shooting.

Conclusion
While RE3 isn't my favorite of the RE games, I do still recommend purely for those Nemesis sections. There's a reason people point to this game when they talk about being chased the entire game in RE games, even if everything else isn't crazy

The real Resident Evil 3! So I had never played this game until till now since I was very young when it came out and I only remember bits and pieces from watching my parents play it. I did play the remake and you can see in my review of that game, I did not enjoy it all really. I even replayed the remake recently after it was super cheap on a steam sale, mainly just for the achievements. Well color me surprised when just after I finish that Capcom drops the GOG ports of the first 3 games onto Steam. So after finally playing through the original game now, what did I think?

Starting with the visuals, I really love how this game looks. Obviously its PS1 graphics so it’s going to look very dated with blocky character models, but I have always loved the PS1’s graphical aesthetic and it definitely gave me a lot of nostalgia. The characters' faces are very static which is the one thing I don’t like, but otherwise the presentation is good in my book and the cinematic cutscenes still look pretty good.

The OST is incredible with the save room music being the most iconic but even the tracks that play while exploring Raccoon City really give off a feeling of bleak hopelessness as the city is all but desolate with the few survivors you come across either being already dead or are about to be killed by a zombie. And the voice acting overall is actually pretty good, with the only real cheesy one imo being Carlos’s voice.

Gameplay wise, it's your classic survival horror fair with the game playing differently depending on if you pick either easy or hard mode. Easy gives you all the best guns at the start and unlimited ink ribbons, so it’s a good mode if you just want to play for the story and then Hard mode is your more traditional Survival horror experience with limited ammo and resources. The ammo crafting is great too with it working basically the same as the remake, only Jill improves over time and will craft more bullets from the powders you pick up.

I also liked how the first half of the game treats Raccoon City like a Spencer Mansion or RPD Police Station, in that you run around, solve puzzles and unlock previously locked doors. And I honestly loved this version of the city. The remake had a decent section like that too, but here I thought it was just the right amount of puzzle solving and combat. After that you move from small area to small area, but the gameplay loop remains the same which is good. But come to think of it, a lot of the sections from the remake are still here, it’s just the remake switched the order of them around and simplified some of them.

Then there’s the two main features of this game being the live selection system and Nemesis himself. The live selection is pretty cool as it gives you different routes through the story with some having you enter different areas depending on the choices you make. It leads to good replay value and I like the idea of it. Then there’s Nemesis who is just as scary as I remember him when watching my parents play the game as a kid. His iconic “Starsssss” line is still great and he’s an absolute tank when you do decide to take him on, often taking tons of grenade rounds to even go down and he’s fast. The only thing I don’t like is his grab move can be quite annoying as he throws Jill around like a ragdoll and you often have to fight with the controls to even get her to stand back up, and by then you have like a split second before Nemesis grabs you again, often using his one hit death grip which lead to many deaths for me.

Then you have the story, which is decent for Resident Evil standards. Obviously picking up and reading the notes helps you understand things better but the actual story told in the cutscenes is straight forward but good. I was actually quite surprised at the encounter you have with that one dude at the start that hides in the truck. In the remake, he just comes off as being difficult as he refuses to go with Jill, but in this version, you actually get some more context to his character which I won’t spoil but it made his cynical, desperate outlook a lot more understandable. Guess it was too much for the remake to include.

Overall, this was an awesome time and I’m glad they have brought the classic trilogy back. I had heard this game was short but it actually took me 10 hours on my first playthrough, when the remake took me at most half that time.

STAUNCH defender of 3. I've always considered RE2 to be Part 1 of the Raccoon City story of the OG RE trilogy, and RE3 is the Part 2 finale where that story comes to a close. 

This is where the transition between survival horror and action truly became complete for the series, but that being said, there's still a decent amount of ammo conversation and deciding when and where to pick your fights--so long as you're playing on Hard. Playing on Easy when you're gifted all these powerful weapons at the start will rob you of the game's intensity otherwise. In many ways, 3's combat feels like a precursor to 4--feeling backed into a corner, taking on waves of enemies, constantly swapping out weapons in your inventory based on enemy type, enemy amount, how much ammo you have for each gun--it's action packed.

Also, ever wanted to explore Raccoon City during the absolute thick of the outbreak? You can in 3--and Raccoon City is absolutely sprawling. In RE1, you explored a claustrophobic mansion. In 2, you explored a claustrophobic but a bit more spacious police department. In RE3, you have the city to explore, with excellent map design that still manages you make you feel trapped in the back alleys and ruined streets of the city, as well as numerous different buildings to explore including public parks, gas stations, stores, the RPD, parking garages, cemeteries, a great hospital section, and an even better Clock Tower segment.

I never understood why people tried to dismiss 3 as "not a true sequel", especially since the 3 was slapped on later as the game was being developed to make it an official sequel, because it already is an official sequel to 2 in all ways. Absolutely positively destroys the mediocre "remake" that came out six years ago. This version absolutely surpasses it.

Resident Evil 3: Nemesis, developed and published by CAPCOM Co., Ltd. with later PC distribution support from GOG.com, remains one of the most intense and distinctive entries in the early survival horror lineage. Rather than simply following the deliberate, puzzle-heavy pacing of its predecessors, this installment leans into urgency and momentum, placing players in a city already on the brink of collapse. The result is a game that feels less like a slow descent into fear and more like a desperate scramble through chaos, where every decision carries weight and hesitation often leads to punishment.

The defining feature of the experience is, without question, the Nemesis itself. More than just a recurring boss, this creature fundamentally reshapes the player’s relationship with the game world. It appears without warning, pursues relentlessly, and forces players to constantly weigh risk versus survival. Fighting it can yield valuable rewards, but doing so consumes precious ammunition and health, while running away risks being cornered later in worse circumstances. This persistent threat transforms otherwise familiar environments into spaces of dread, as even safe routes can become deadly in an instant. Few antagonists in gaming have achieved this level of psychological pressure, and Nemesis earns its reputation as one of the most iconic enemies in the medium.

Gameplay builds on the foundation of earlier titles but introduces key refinements that subtly push the series forward. Movement feels more responsive thanks to the addition of a quick-turn maneuver, and the dodge system—though sometimes inconsistent—adds a layer of skill-based evasion that rewards timing and awareness. The inclusion of an ammunition crafting system also gives players more agency over their resources, allowing them to tailor their approach depending on playstyle. These systems collectively make the game feel slightly more action-oriented, yet it never abandons the careful resource management and tension that define survival horror. Inventory decisions remain meaningful, and the constant scarcity ensures that even minor encounters can feel significant.

Visually, the game represents a strong evolution of the pre-rendered aesthetic that defined the era. The ruined streets of Raccoon City are richly detailed, filled with environmental storytelling that conveys the scale of the disaster without excessive exposition. Burning cars, shattered storefronts, and abandoned barricades all contribute to a sense of place that feels convincingly lived-in and tragically destroyed. Character models are noticeably improved, particularly Jill Valentine, whose animations and expressions lend more personality to the narrative. Combined with effective sound design—ranging from distant groans to sudden crashes—the atmosphere remains thick with tension from beginning to end.

The narrative itself focuses less on grand revelations and more on immediacy. It places players in the middle of a crisis already in motion, emphasizing survival over discovery. The “Live Selection” mechanic enhances this by introducing timed choices that influence how certain situations unfold. While these branching moments do not radically alter the overarching story, they add a welcome sense of agency and replay value, encouraging multiple playthroughs to see different outcomes. This design choice reinforces the game’s central theme: survival is not just about skill, but about decisions made under pressure.

Despite its strengths, the game is not without flaws. Its shorter length compared to its predecessor can make the experience feel somewhat condensed, particularly for players expecting a longer, more expansive campaign. Some elements, such as voice acting and certain scripted sequences, show their age, and the game occasionally leans heavily on familiar assets and ideas from earlier entries. However, these shortcomings are largely overshadowed by the intensity and focus of the overall design, which prioritizes pacing and replayability over sheer scale.

In retrospect, Resident Evil 3: Nemesis (1999) stands as a bold refinement of the classic survival horror formula. It trades some of the slower, methodical exploration of earlier games for a more aggressive and unpredictable experience, anchored by one of the most memorable antagonists in gaming history. Its mechanical tweaks, atmospheric design, and relentless pacing ensure that it remains engaging even decades later. While it may not be the longest or most narratively complex entry in the series, its ability to sustain tension and deliver a consistently gripping experience secures its place as a standout title in the genre.

‎The project is in development and has shown promising early alpha footage.
‎Another, separate project mentioned is the RE3 Extended Edition by modder dragonleo, which focuses on opening up areas for better interconnection.

(I know some people can't stand tank controls but I grew up with them so I'm used to it and even some indie games these days like Signalis uses them).

I was very sad about the treatment the remake got and I know some people loved it still but I just couldn't. 

The opening is still one of the coolest Resident Evil intros. The open world aspect of the city with the puzzles and figuring out how to navigate the city and survive is a big part of the fun of this game. Having to make quick choices on how to deal with Nemesis when he shows up in an event. Or even as he suddenly drops out of nowhere while you're trying to do some mundane task (Like how Mr. X was in RE2R and how he should have been handled in RE3R instead of being fully scripted). The clock tower. Can't forget it, it's one of my favorite sections in the game. The mercenaries mode is also really dang good in this one.

Anyways I'm excited to play through this game again. I know all the others who really loved the original are every bit as happy to have gotten this surprise as I was. And for people who haven't played the original before I'm glad they'll get a chance now to experience it. Though I know still it won't be up some people's alley due to the controls. But for those who don't mind it and like the older RE games you won't regret getting this one I guarantee.

Still one of the greatest survival horror games of all time, 27 years later. Alien Isolation? You have Nemesis to than for that! RE2 Remake? Who do you think Mr. X took his gimmick from baby? Ms. Valentine is also a total killer here, fighting her way out of Raccoon City in an incredibly impractical outfit, serving through the horror. 

In all seriousness, this game is one of my favorite games of all time, and it still makes me (V) jolt to this day. Nemmy running at you and WWE clotheslining you into the Danger status will never not make me jump out of my skin. This may not be the purest form of Survival Horror ever made (that would be the RE1 Remake thank you very much) but if you want a game that will challenge your survival instincts and force you to think on your brown survival horror girly booted feet, RE3: Nemesis is for you!

Love this game. At time of writing, it's Day 2 of the Steam release and I already finished a playthrough. Easily my favorite of the original trilogy on PS1. The third game does away with a lot of the obtuse puzzles and backtracking of the previous games (for the most part) and delivers a more streamlined experience.

The new quick-turn and auto-aim features really help to mitigate the clunkiness of the tank controls and give the game more of an action-y edge. Hit feedback is cathartic and satisfying, so blasting zombies never gets old. The game has tons of replay value, with choices at certain sections that offer small branches in the story, as well as certain item pickups being randomized when you start the game. The ammo crafting system means you have flexibility in which weapons you want to use in a given playthrough, with the system even having a hidden experience mechanic where Jill can get more bullets with each craft, eventually being able to make upgraded ammo. My only major complaint is that there are some (admittedly rare) situations where Jill can be thrown to the ground and you have to mash buttons for her to get up again. Mashing buttons always sucks.

The games tone teeters between depressing and oppressive, exploring a city that is already lost, all the while trying to evade Nemesis, who was easily the most iconic villian the series had up to that point. Jill is a great character, and the rest of the cast is decent, and you'll really feel for them as they try to make their desparate escape. The excellent pre-rendered backgrounds are full of detail, and there are files scattered about that contain often tragic stories that really nail the tone.

Everything about the sound design is amazing. The mournful tones of several tracks ending with the leitmotif of the Nemesis theme, reminding you that he's never far away. Combine this with the various ambient sounds: The scream of a survivor, just beyond saving. The sounds of a corpse being devoured by monsters, just off-screen. The grim wailing of distant zombies, carried on the wind. It's all just so moody and effective and I love every part of it.

I've finished this game dozens of times and I can't praise it enough. Happy to finally see this one on Steam with some new features compared to the PS1 release. They're asking a reasonable price for it compared to a lot of other companies' re-released or remastered output costing nearly the amount of a new triple-A release (Looking at you Square Enix).

Thumbs up. Get it. Play it. Hope you like it even half as much as I do.

You removed it from 4R and the game now runs at nearly 200fps on my PC, imagine how well this could run if you just dropped that performance-killing nightmare?

Now, onto the game. First things first, the Steam Overlay doesn't work and I suspect that's because this is a straight GoG port.  I would love a patch that restores the overlay functionality so I can screenshot the various Live Select choices, and my end-clear rankings for this wonderful game.

Now, if you're new to RE3 this is the pinnacle.  Non-stop-gameplay, a broad inventory, a dodge move that's very unforgiving yet immensely rewarding if you can learn it, and a brutal and ruthless Pursuer that will never stop hunting you until you are dead.  CAPCOM nowadays thinks "taking away your weapons and making you stand in a corner while a scripted unkillable enemy patrols" is scary, but Nemesis is scary, at least the OG version of him in this game is.  He will come at you when you least expect it, he'll toy with you, he'll square up to you even if he knows you have Carlos helping you --- he does not care, and that to me makes him the scariest RE monster to this very day.  RE3 started the high-octane action trend often attributed to 4 and I've always thought it was a good thing.  RE3 birthed quick turns, environmental hazards, a choice-based live select system we've never seen since, and the most costumes of any RE game for its protagonist.   There's just so much game here, and it doesn't bog you down with scripted walking talking sections or hospital wave defence; you're in the midst of a city besieged by a virus in the middle of a hot raging summer. Jill dresses light for the heat, she needs to be nimble and on her feet at all times. Everything is diagetic and works so damn well. I could gush about this game forever.  This and the original Halo Trilogy are the only games where I even recommend the novella, the S.D. Perry book for RE3 contextualises the game with so much richness and depth you begin to think about it as you play it for yourself. 

Unlike the 2020 remake, here we get the brilliant US Army vs TYRANTs last stand at the Dead Factory, Raccoon Park, the Hospital in all of its glory, and our beloved Clock Tower.   The amount of content in this game is staggering and I'll always be sour that CAPCOM internally view CV as the "true" RE3, because this game earned the number and conclusion to the Raccoon Trilogy and then some.  This is the only RE still to this day where even if you complete it for the 100th time, you feel like you and Jill just went through Hell together and survived. It's majestic.

"It all began as an ordinary day in September. An ordinary day in Raccoon City. A city controlled by Umbrella. No one dared to oppose them. That and the lack of strength would ultimately lead to their destruction. I suppose they had to suffer the consequences of their actions but there would be no forgiveness, if only they had had the courage to fight... But it's true that once the wheels of justice began to turn, nothing can stop them. Nothing. It was Raccoon City's last chance... And my last chance, my last escape..."

Personally for me, RE3 OG is the best RE game of all time and for good reasons. 

First of all, the atmosphere. You explore quite a bit of the city and you just feel the dread and hopelessness that surrounds it. The ambience you hear of zombies who howl, because they still have a bit of conciousness in them, the crows cawing, the wind blowing, you can't beat this atmosphere. 

Second of all, Jill herself. If we were to think about the true "strong and independent female character" besides Lara Croft, Jill Valentine is definitely up there. She isn't there to bully male characters, she isn't there to flex how badass she is, she's just there to survive and do whatever it takes. She feels fear, she knows that the situation she's in is hopeless and yet, she doesn't give up. She also cares for others and doesn't want to leave any survivors behind. That's how you make a strong female character. Not to mention that she was one of the first female leads in video games in general. All in all, Jill is still one of the most iconic female protagonists in video game history.

Next thing is the Nemesis (The REAL Nemesis, not that cheap copy in RE3 Remake). The first stalker enemy in RE series and I might say that he's still the best (Mr.X in RE2 Remake was cool and all, but he wasn't the main antagonist). He's there just to eliminate STARS members and does everything to reach that goal. His iconic growls and "STARS" line is still carved into my brain after all those years. His boss fights are amazing and I think that Capcom has yet to make another beast as iconic as Nemesis. 

We also have the music, which is one of the best in the series by far. Hell, you know the soundtrack is amazing, if even the options screen has a memorable track. The save room theme, Nemesis theme, City of Ruin, Nemesis Final Metamorphosis, The Doomed City, Hellish Agony, I can just go on and on and name every single track in the OST, because all of them are amazing. The PS1 era really had an amazing music, no?

We also have small things like the choice system, where in some situations you have to choose one of the two choices that display on the screen. One choice can lead to better results than the other, so you have to think carefully about it. You also have a lot of choices regarding Nemesis, whether you will fight him or not. If you decide to fight him and manage to defeat him (it's not as easy as it sounds) the game rewards you for it and you will get a waaay better equipment.

All in all, RE3 OG for me is the peak Resident Evil game and It sucks that the remake for it is the worst of them all and it can just wish to be as great as the OG. Hell, even Capcom knows it, since they made DLC for every single RE Engine RE game, but not for 3 Remake lmao. But hey, at least we finally have a way to buy RE3 OG, whether it's here on Steam or on GOG. 10/10 game, I will still play it, even if I'm on my deathbed.

Overall, Resident Evil 3 remains a classic in the survival horror genre. It’s a game that not only stands the test of time but also brings back many fond memories. I’d recommend it to anyone looking for a thrilling experience, but I can’t help but wish Capcom had taken the chance to update it with some achievements.

The one and only RE 3 is back! THE best.

We've finally got the remake for Resident Evil 3 and it's everything we could have hoped for. No, not everything. More. Not only it fixes all the problems the original had it also add plenty of content, here's the list (it's a long one).

   - We need to begin with Nemesis himself. For this remake, it's clear why Capcom wanted to put his name in the title: they improved him in every way possible. Remember how in the original Nemesis hunted Jill for like 5 minutes? Screw that, now he hunts you the *entire* game. He is relentless and very clever. Way more threatening, imposing and dangerous. Gone were the days you could drop him with a single grenade. Now to defeat him you must give everything you have, and that might not be enough. He is very tough, but fair. To make up for this added difficulty his drops are much more interesting (new guns, health items and even infinite ammo!). Another very smart change is to make him humanoid for 99% of the game. What were the original team thinking when they changed him into a dog midway through the game?! I do miss him having a flamethrower though (he shows up with a Rocket Launcher more times though) and I have a soft spot for his original design (nose included). But all in all, they took a mediocre set piece boss and made him into a true stalker, the best I ever experienced in a game. STARS!
   - There is an entire new gameplay segment between Jill apartment and you getting to the train.
Raccoon City is *grealy* expanded. It's much more open and there are many more places you can go. To get the train moving it's not simply about going to the power station, you have to collect a number of itens all over the city, often with Nemesis pursuing you. 
   - There is a second boss (I won't spoil it to you!)
   - Remember the Clock Tower? That building you could see in the distance when you fought dog Nemesis? It's now an entire map! I ♥♥♥♥ you not. They took a single background building and made it into a mini-Spencer Mansion, full of puzzles and a superb atmosphere. It's gonna be a fan favorite for sure.
   - They added a park which although not very good is better than the sewers (which were thankfully removed, more original content, less copy and paste from RE2).
   - That Nest 2.0 RE2 clone? Now it's a special kind of Umbrella facility, it adds much more personality to this game. 
   - There is a new mini-game! It's called The Mercenaries and it's very fun. It adds much replayability. 
   - There are way more weapons and skins for Jill (7 in total). New ammo types and a much improved ammo crafting mechanic, better than in all other RE titles.
   - There is a live-selection mechanics that allow you to make choices in critical moments, which led to different outcomes and make replays much more varied. It even changes the story (there are more than one ending now)
   - Some story elements were tweaked for the better, I don't want to spoil too much, but now we visit the RPD as Jill. Think about it, doesn't it make much more sense? Seeing the place she spend so much of her days at, going to the STARS office as one of the few lasting members of the team and... no, I won't even talk about *that* moment! You will know when you see it (and scream, probably). 

I could go on, but there is thing they add that is more important than all of those, and it's a bit harder to describe: a soul. The original RE3 was a spiritually small game, the RE formula from RE2 and RE1 was gone, there was basically no puzzles, inventory management, route planning, and all that. But the madmen at Capcom did the impossible, they added a big soul for this remake. The puzzles, enemies (there are new enemies!), key itens, a more open map... it all combines to give you that classic, fantastic Resident Evil experience, but in a more action-y way. And it all works not only because all of those mechanics function well, but because Nemesis. Really, I couldn't make him justice enough here. He is the element that holds everything together, making every decision count and every escape a desperate one. 

It's not all good news though, there are a few things that are worse in the remake. The graphics are slightly worse, I'm not sure why. But you will only notice if you look really close. Carlos and especially Nikolai aren't as good as they were in the original, although there are some scenes with them with are very good. I prefer Jill's characterization from the original, but I expect a lot of people will prefer this version, regardless, in terms of combat and wits she is way more capable here as Nemesis is a much more demanding foe (she reminds me of Jason Bourne, always thinking on her feet and using the environment to her advantage in clever ways). The voice acting is a bit worse alas, they should have all the voice cast from the original returning, but maybe they were not available. But that's about it for the bad part, really trivial compared to all the good.

God, this was a long review. But as someone who was a bit disappointed by the original RE3 and hoped they would remake it one day like the other RE titles, this was beyond my wildest dreams. It's so, so good. It took something that you had to force yourself to like and turned it into a classic. We finally got the RE3 we dreamed of!

I absolutely love this game. My 2nd favorite RE game, and IMO, the best of the first 3 OG games. 

If you’ve ever see comments made by the community about how the remake of 3 didn’t live up to the OG, then play this right here and see why. It’s criminal how much the remake cut compared to this game. 

There’s a good blend of action and puzzle solving. Being able to explore a good chunk of Raccoon city is great. The game has a really unique mechanic where you get to make a decision between two choices, usually during a fight or flight moment, And the result (while not making significant changes to the story) does provide some really cool outcomes. This also provides replay-ability so you can see the different outcomes. 
Nemesis proves here why he is still the ultimate, most scary stalker enemy in the series. You can just be going through an enemy free area, and then hear a door open, and start hearing heavy footsteps Sprinting in your direction. The game also introduces a dodge/shove mechanic, which can be a bit finicky, but when you pull it off it’s very helpful and satisfying. 

This game was also the first to introduce Mercenaries mode. It’s not as fleshed out as it is in future titles, but it is there. 

I urge every Resident Evil to give this a try if they haven’t. A very underrrated title that deserves its time to shine. No matter how much CapCom tries to hide it in the shadows behind that dissapointing Remake.

The release of the classic games is a great surprise, and I do think that it is a great way to get acquainted with them: you don't have to use emulators or search for a copy, you just pay $5.00 per game and you are good to go!
But is it actually a good choice considering everything which goes on underneath?
 
The good part - there is now a chance to experience the original RE3, rather than the Remake which has some part of the content missing. Also, Mercenaries mode and all the costumes coming along with the game! Also, nostalgia!

The underwhelming part? 
- No achievement system
- No cloud saves
- The Enigma Protector DRM [b](WHY?)[/b]
- Pixelated image (no proper aspect ratio, no upscale, and I DO NOT mean AI nor RTX/DLSS as some might think).
- Very little options to tweak the game's settings (meaning all you can do is reassign controls and change the resolution, and all that with the requirement of discovering that the settings menu is to be opened by pressing F1, which is not stated anywhere). 

There is actually a launcher coming with the game, which is... you guessed it, useless, because seemingly the settings you apply don't even work accordingly.
If you open the in-game settings menu, you'll acknowledge that the resolution is not what you have chosen in the launcher, and that there are actually controls settings with the opportunity to remap them, which are... not in the launcher!

I do think that there is a need for some tweaks post-release. There is no need for a full-on remaster (it actually depends on what one considers a remaster...) since we have a remake already, but having some more options in the launcher, removing the DRM from a game which is 27 years old and adding some achievements would be great.

Also, it would be a great idea to include the manual, because for many it would be impossible to navigate in a 1999 game menus nowadays.

Keep in mind, this game is on GOG for quite a while now (since September 2024), and it doesn't have any DRM whatsoever.
The cherry on top? 
"This re-released version of the game was co-developed by GOG.". In the official Steam description.
